name: Amoxicillin
route_note: Usually oral capsules, tablets or suspension; IV formulations are available in some countries (not the US).

discovery.note: Developed as an orally better-absorbed analogue of ampicillin by adding a para-hydroxyl group to the side chain.

tagline: The world's workhorse oral penicillin for respiratory, ear and urinary infections
summary: Amoxicillin is a semi-synthetic aminopenicillin introduced by Beecham in 1972. Better absorbed orally than ampicillin, it is one of the most widely prescribed antibiotics worldwide and a first-line WHO Access antibiotic for common community infections.
mechanism: Like other penicillins, amoxicillin binds and inactivates penicillin-binding proteins, blocking the transpeptidation step of peptidoglycan cross-linking and causing lysis of dividing bacteria.

Its amino group improves penetration through Gram-negative porins, extending activity to many Haemophilus influenzae, Escherichia coli and Enterococcus faecalis strains, but it is destroyed by beta-lactamases; it is therefore often combined with clavulanic acid.
uses: Acute otitis media, sinusitis and streptococcal pharyngitis
Urinary tract infections caused by susceptible organisms
Helicobacter pylori eradication (with a proton pump inhibitor and another antibiotic)
Early Lyme disease and endocarditis prophylaxis in some guidelines

history.title: Ampicillin precursor
history.detail: Beecham launches ampicillin, the first broad-spectrum penicillin, from which amoxicillin was derived.

history.title: Launch
history.detail: Amoxicillin is introduced in the United Kingdom as Amoxil.

history.title: Combination with clavulanate
history.detail: Amoxicillin-clavulanic acid (Augmentin) is launched to overcome beta-lactamase resistance.

history.title: WHO AWaRe
history.detail: WHO's Essential Medicines List groups antibiotics into Access, Watch and Reserve; amoxicillin is a key Access antibiotic.

history.title: Paediatric shortages
history.detail: Surges in streptococcal and respiratory infections cause shortages of amoxicillin suspension in the US, UK and Europe in 2022–2023.

pk.bioavailability: about 70–90% orally, largely unaffected by food

serious: Stevens-Johnson syndrome and other severe skin reactions

facts: A maculopapular rash is very common when amoxicillin or ampicillin is given to patients with infectious mononucleosis (Epstein-Barr virus) and does not necessarily indicate true penicillin allergy.
Amoxicillin is among the most frequently prescribed antibiotics for children worldwide.
